questions.prompt: Per-run SD 6, mean of 12 seeds reported. Standard error? (3 decimals)
Per-run SD 2, mean of 10 seeds. 95% tolerance for the difference between two independent re-runs? (2 decimals)
How many seeds per run set are needed so two re-runs agree within 1 point (95%) when sigma=2? Use n >= (1.96*sqrt(2)*sigma/1)^2, rounded up.
A replication differs from your result by 1.0 point; your 95% tolerance is 2.5. How should you read this?
options: A failed replication, since the numbers are not identical to the original.
Proof the replication was wrong, because it differs from the reported number.
Consistent with the original within seed variability.
Proof the original was wrong, because the results do not agree exactly.
questions.explanation: Difference inside the tolerance is expected.

questions.prompt: Which statement about floating-point addition is correct?
options: It is not associative, so the order of a parallel reduction can change low-order digits.
It is exact for all doubles, so the order of a reduction never changes the sum.
Its order never matters, since the result is rounded to the same value at the end.
Only integers have rounding errors, since floating-point values are stored exactly.

questions.prompt: In IEEE double precision, what does (1e16 - 1e16) + 1.0 evaluate to?
Setting random.seed(0) is not enough to make a PyTorch training run reproducible because:
options: Python ignores seeds when it is run on a GPU, so the run changes every time.
Seeds are only meant for testing, and a training run cannot be made deterministic.
Other generators (NumPy, framework, workers) and GPU kernels have their own randomness.
random.seed has no effect on any number generator, so seeds cannot make runs repeat.
questions.explanation: Each library keeps its own generator state.

questions.prompt: Which environment specification best supports reproducibility?
options: Exact versions in a lock file (ideally with hashes), or a container pinned by digest.
A screenshot of the package list, which shows the versions that were installed.
'pip install latest', which always gives the newest and therefore best-tested version.
A note saying 'Python 3', since the interpreter version is the only thing that matters.

questions.prompt: A figure was edited by hand in a drawing program after plotting. What is the main reproducibility issue?
options: The final figure cannot be regenerated from raw data by script.
The file is too large to be stored together with the code in the repository.
The colours changed, so the figure no longer matches the one in the paper.
None; the plot was produced by a script, so the result is still reproducible.

Statistical: results agree within seed variance, e.g. GPU or parallel reductions.
